record.original_question: Rerandomized subsampled trigonometric transforms: Assume that $n = Omega( r)$. Prove or disprove: The rerandomized SRHT of dimension $k = O(r/epsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with $alpha = 1-epsilon$ and $beta = 1+epsilon$.

evidence.quote: Assume that $n = \Omega(\log r)$. Prove or disprove: The rerandomized SRHT of dimension $k = \mathcal{O}(r/\varepsilon^2)$ is an oblivious subspace embedding with $\alpha = 1-\varepsilon$ and $\beta = 1+\varepsilon$.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H_n \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ denote the (normalized) Walsh–Hadamard matrix on $n$ points (assume $n$ is a power of two), so that $H_n^\top H_n = I_n$. For a positive integer $k \le n$ define the subsampled randomized Hadamard transform (SRHT) by
$$ S \;=\; \sqrt{n/k}\, P\, H_n\, D, $$
where $D \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is a random diagonal sign matrix whose diagonal entries are i.i.d. uniform on $\{\pm 1\}$, and $P \in \{0,1\}^{k \times n}$ is a uniformly random row-subsampling matrix that selects $k$ rows of $H_n D$ (with or without replacement).

A rerandomized SRHT of dimension $k$ is the random linear map obtained by drawing an independent fresh copy $(D, P)$ of the SRHT for each input vector (equivalently, the sketch is allowed to be redrawn for each query rather than fixed once and applied to all of a subspace simultaneously).

For parameters $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, a positive integer $r$, and constants $0 < \alpha \le \beta$, a random matrix $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$ is called an oblivious subspace embedding for $r$-dimensional subspaces with distortion $(\alpha, \beta)$ if, for every fixed $r$-dimensional linear subspace $V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$ \Pr\!\Big[\, \alpha \|x\|_2 \le \|Sx\|_2 \le \beta \|x\|_2 \ \text{for all } x \in V \,\Big] \;\ge\; 1 - \delta, $$
for some absolute constant $\delta \in (0,1)$ (e.g. $\delta = 1/3$).

Assume $n = \Omega(\log r)$. Prove or disprove the following statement: there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that for every $r$-dimensional subspace and every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, the rerandomized SRHT with embedding dimension
$$ k \;=\; C\, r / \varepsilon^2 $$
is an oblivious subspace embedding with $\alpha = 1 - \varepsilon$ and $\beta = 1 + \varepsilon$.
artifact.category_tag: randomized numerical linear algebra / subspace embeddings
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2025) establishes that sparse oblivious subspace embeddings can attain the optimal embedding dimension $m = \Theta(r/\varepsilon^2)$ (resolving the Nelson–Nguyen conjecture up to sub-polylogarithmic factors), and standard SRHT analyses give $k = \tilde O(r/\varepsilon^2)$ with extra $\log$ factors. However, no source directly confirms that the specifically rerandomized SRHT achieves the clean optimal $k = O(r/\varepsilon^2)$ bound under the stated assumption $n = \Omega(\log r)$. The status of this exact statement could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Embedding Dimension for Sparse Subspace Embeddings
status_evidence.snippet: Sparse OSEs achieving optimal embedding dimension m = O(d/eps^2).
status_evidence.claim: Optimal embedding dimension r/eps^2 is achievable by sparse oblivious sketches, related but not identical to rerandomized SRHT.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Subspace Embeddings: Resolving Nelson-Nguyen Conjecture Up to Sub-Polylogarithmic Factors
status_evidence.snippet: Construction with O~(d/eps^2) rows and O~(log d/eps) nonzeros per column giving an OSE.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work resolves optimal OSE dimension up to sub-polylog factors, but does not specifically address rerandomized SRHT.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Oblivious Subspace Embeddings with Near-optimal Sparsity
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal OSE with near-optimal sparsity per column.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates active research on optimal OSE dimensions; rerandomized SRHT specifically not addressed.
